title: Evaluating a Deterministic‑Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 paired intent→configuration tasks; preregistration cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) to test whether a minimal guarded pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation (gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration versus plain single‑shot generation. Execution (planned episodes 600, completed 600, model_calls_used 301) produced baseline = 299/300 valid configurations (99.667%) and guarded = 300/300 valid configurations (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single permitted automated repair call corrected the sole initially invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; 95% Clopper–Pearson CI = [0.025, 1.0]). The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40 (relative reduction target: 50%); the observed near‑ceiling baseline invalidates that planning assumption. We report the preregistered design, execution accounting, archived validator/repair traces, a short post‑hoc sensitivity statement using the archived contingency counts and CI, and implications for future confirmatory NetOps evaluations.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation can accelerate NetOps but poses operational risks when generated changes are missequenced, incomplete, or otherwise unsafe. Recent surveys and system proposals recommend generate→verify→repair architectures combining LLM generators with deterministic validators or simulators to reduce misconfiguration risk. We designed a narrowly scoped preregistered paired experiment to quantify whether a minimal guarded pipeline—a frozen deterministic validator plus ≤1 automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to unguarded single‑shot generation. Our contribution is a preregistered paired test (N=300) with deterministically generated task seeds, archival of model outputs and validator/repair traces, and an evidence‑grounded analysis of statistical and methodological factors (notably baseline ceiling effects and sampling semantics) shaping detectability of safety gains.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents both promise and risk for LLMs in NetOps tasks. Empirical demos and surveys show LLMs can translate operator intent to configuration templates but emphasize hallucination, misordering, and overconfidence as key hazards. Cross‑domain studies (medical/QA/code) report that retrieval augmentation, deterministic verifiers, and automated repair loops measurably improve grounding and reduce factual errors. Architectural literature for NetOps increasingly advocates deterministic validators as floor‑safety nets and generate→verify→repair patterns for agentic workflows. However, the literature contains few preregistered A/B experiments that quantify misconfiguration‑rate reductions from a minimal validator+single‑repair pipeline across a deterministically generated paired test set; our experiment aims to fill that targeted empirical gap with fully archived artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and hypotheses: We preregistered the study as cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1 and specified two confirmatory hypotheses: H1 — guarded pipeline reduces first‑pass misconfiguration rate by ≥50% (relative) versus plain single‑shot generation; H2 — one or fewer automated repair iterations recover ≥75% of initially invalid configurations. The preregistration's planning assumption used a baseline pass rate = 0.40 for power calculations and mapped a 50% relative reduction in fail rate to an absolute pass‑rate increase from 40%→70% (this preregistered baseline assumption is recorded in the preregistration artifact; see the Disclosure Statement for the preregistration SHA). Design and sampling: a paired within‑task design with 300 deterministic seeds produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each seed yielded two paired episodes: baseline (single‑shot generation) and guarded (same initial candidate validated using a frozen deterministic validator and up to one automated repair attempt). The execution contract fixed initial_generation_calls_per_task=1 and maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1 and declared generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (the archived runtime control that caused the same sampled candidate to be presented to both arms). Model and runtime: declared model = gpt-5-mini; execution used provider adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and frozen deterministic validator/repair = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Primary estimand and test: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact McNemar (two‑sided, α=0.05). Analysis plan and preregistered sensitivity: primary analysis used the exact McNemar on paired binary pass/fail outcomes and reported absolute and relative reductions with 95% CIs; missingness and failure treatments followed the preregistered policies. All raw responses, per‑task validator traces, repair traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts were archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 600, complete pairs = 300, model_calls_used = 301; provider audit reported stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}. Primary outcomes (archived analysis artifacts): baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%); paired contingency: n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair usage and H2: the guarded pipeline invoked the single permitted repair call once and corrected the sole initially invalid configuration; hence repair recovery point estimate = 1.0 (1/1). The preregistered H1 (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported because the observed baseline was near ceiling. Post‑hoc sensitivity statement: with only one discordant pair (n10=1, n01=0) the data provide negligible inferential leverage to detect the preregistered effect size. The observed bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.01] bounds the absolute paired difference to at most 0.01 under the run's sampling semantics; therefore, the run cannot rule in or out larger practical improvements in harder task regimes and lacks the discordant‑pair counts needed to achieve the preregistered power for a 30 percentage‑point absolute change. Secondary and exploratory diagnostics (archived): contamination checks flagged no deterministic exact duplicates among preregistered seeds; no model or provider failures occurred under the preregistered retry policy; exclusions or replacements were not executed. Representative per‑task validator traces and the single repair trace are archived for inspection in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion: Operational lessons and methodological implications. (1) Ceiling effects and effect‑size alignment: the preregistered power plan assumed baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicts that assumption and removed headroom for measurable relative improvement. Confirmatory designs must align preregistered effect sizes with plausible baseline error rates for the chosen task bank. (2) Paired sampling semantics matter: the archived runtime literal generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" intentionally reused the same sampled candidate across paired arms. That practice reduces variability in generated candidates but increases within‑pair correlation and reduces the number of discordant pairs that McNemar uses for inference. Future preregistrations should explicitly define whether paired arms draw independently or reuse a shared candidate and adjust power planning accordingly. (3) Repair evidence precision: though the single repair call succeeded (1/1), the small denominator yields a wide Clopper–Pearson interval [0.025, 1.0]; estimating repair effectiveness precisely requires substantially more initial failures—produced either by harder task banks or by adversarial stress testing. (4) Design recommendations: to evaluate operational readiness for autonomous change execution, future experiments should (a) increase task difficulty or introduce adversarial cases to raise baseline failure counts, (b) consider independent paired draws (or explicitly plan for shared‑candidate semantics), (c) broaden validator fidelity (dynamic emulation in addition to deterministic constraint checks), (d) permit multi‑iteration repair policies where appropriate, and (e) test multiple model families to probe generality. (5) Archival transparency: our run archives model responses, per‑task validator and repair traces, the execution manifest, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible reanalysis and facilitate more challenging follow‑on experiments.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (N=300) using gpt‑5‑mini and a frozen deterministic validator with ≤1 automated repair iteration, baseline single‑shot generation was near‑ceiling (299/300) and the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs; a single repair call corrected the only observed failure but did not yield a statistically detectable improvement for the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis. The run demonstrates that task difficulty, paired sampling semantics (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"), validator coverage, and baseline error rates jointly determine whether guarded pipelines produce detectable safety gains in confirmatory designs. We release full archived artifacts (model responses, validator/repair traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts) to support reproducibility and to inform follow‑on experiments that probe harder operational regimes and alternative sampling semantics.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.
The preregistered power plan assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicts that assumption and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction.

Sampling semantics (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available to McNemar inference.

Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences of configurations were not executed and remain unmeasured.

H2 repair‑success evidence is based on a single initially invalid case (1/1 → 100%), yielding a wide Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]; larger counts of initial failures are required to estimate repair effectiveness precisely.
